demoWms.pageSubtitle: Receiving with scanning, rule-based putaway, inventory by lot and expiry, picking waves, packing with a shipping label, own-fleet routing, returns and 3PL pre-invoicing. Everything runs in your browser with a sample operation.

meta.title: WMS and warehouse logistics
meta.seoTitle: WMS demo: receiving, lot inventory, picking and shipping
meta.seoDescription: Interactive WMS demo with sample data: receiving with scanning, rule-based putaway, inventory by lot and expiry (FEFO), picking waves, packing with a simulated shipping label, own-fleet routing, returns and 3PL pre-invoicing in Colombian pesos. Tailored to your warehouse during implementation.

shell.company: Fictitious logistics operator (3PL) with three warehouses and three fictitious clients. Your changes are saved only in this browser until the end of the day.
shell.notSaved: Could not save in this browser
shell.resetText: Your changes (receipts, waves, labels, counts, returns…) are deleted and today’s sample operation is generated again.
shell.resetDone: Demo reset with today’s sample operation

tour.title: Suggested walkthrough (CEDI Funza)
tour.subtitle: Six steps, about 4 minutes. Each step checks itself off when you do it.

received.title: Receive PO OC-24871
received.text: Simulate the truck unloading (or scan) and close the receipt: the demo detects the shortage.

putaway.title: Put away what you received
putaway.text: Confirm or change the rule-based location (rotation, volume, FEFO).

wave.title: Release a wave
wave.text: Select the orders with stock (or those due today), pick a strategy and release the wave.

picked.title: Pick the wave
picked.text: In the picker view, scan the location and the product at each stop.

shipped.title: Pack and create the label
shipped.text: Verify, weigh, compare carriers and create the shipping label.

delivered.title: Deliver with proof
delivered.text: In the driver app, record the delivery with name, signature and photo.

wave.name: By order (wave)
wave.desc: The wave’s orders are picked one by one: one trip per order. Simplest, but it means the most walking.

batch.name: Batch
batch.desc: A single trip for all the wave’s orders, adding up quantities per location. They are split by order at packing.

zone.name: By zone
zone.desc: Each picker works their zone (A, B or C) at the same time; orders are consolidated at packing.

cluster.name: Cluster
cluster.desc: A cart with up to 6 totes: each tote is an order and the locations of those orders are visited together.

dashboard.title: Today’s dashboard · {wh}
dashboard.subtitle: Indicators calculated from the sample operation. Click one to go to its screen.

kpi.dueToday: {n, plural, =0 {None due today} one {# pending with today’s cutoff} other {# pending with today’s cutoff}}
kpi.inTransit: {n, plural, one {# shipment in progress} other {# shipments in progress}}
kpi.accuracyHint: {n, plural, one {# count recorded} other {# counts recorded}}
kpi.putawayHint: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing to put away} one {# putaway task} other {# putaway tasks}}
kpi.expiredHint: {n, plural, =0 {None expired} one {# expired} other {# expired}}

dashboard.note: Indicators are recalculated with every action you take in the demo. In your project they come from your real operation.
dashboard.noActivity: No activity in this warehouse yet.

alerts.expired: {n, plural, one {# expired lot} other {# expired lots}}: review and write them off
alerts.expiring: {n, plural, one {# lot expires} other {# lots expire}} in the next 30 days
alerts.putaway: {n, plural, one {# putaway task} other {# putaway tasks}} pending
alerts.counts: {n, plural, one {# count scheduled} other {# counts scheduled}} for today
alerts.exceptions: {n, plural, one {# shipment} other {# shipments}} with an exception
alerts.rmas: {n, plural, one {# open return} other {# open returns}}

log.poClosedIssues: Receipt closed with {issues, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}}: {po}
log.pickShort: Shortage at {bin} (order {order}): {qty} u.; {realloc} u. reallocated from another lot

receiving.listSubtitle: What you expect to receive and what was already received.
receiving.none: No purchase orders in this warehouse.
receiving.scannerNote: Works with USB or Bluetooth barcode scanners that type like a keyboard (they read the code and send Enter). Scanning with the phone camera is added during implementation.
receiving.unloadNote: “Simulate unloading” records what the sample truck actually brings (it may not match the PO). When you close, the demo compares against the PO and creates the putaway tasks.
receiving.scanUnknown: Code {code} is not in this PO: it is recorded as an issue

issue.wrongSku: {qty} u. with a code that is not in the PO

putaway.title: Putaway
putaway.subtitle: Location suggested by simple, explainable rules. You can change it before confirming.
putaway.none: No putaway tasks in this warehouse.
putaway.allDone: Everything received is already put away.

rules.sameSku: There are already lots of this SKU at that location: they are kept together and the picker takes the one that expires first (FEFO).
rules.highRotation: Class A (fast movers): zone A, the closest to the shipping dock.
rules.bulky: Bulky or heavy product: zone C.
rules.reserve: Medium or slow movers: reserve zone B.
rules.overflow: No space in the preferred zone: first free location.
rules.damaged: Damaged units: they go to quarantine until reviewed.

putaway.note: The rules (rotation, volume and expiry) are configured in your project for your warehouse. It is not artificial intelligence: they are rules you can audit.

crossdock.title: Cross-dock
crossdock.subtitle: Goods move from the receiving dock to the shipping dock without being stored.
crossdock.waitingText: When you receive this PO, the goods go straight to order {order}.
crossdock.note: The label is created with the warehouse’s preferred carrier if it covers the destination; otherwise with the cheapest one. Simulated in the demo.

kits.title: Kits (kitting)
kits.subtitle: Assemble kits from their components: they are consumed by FEFO and the kit enters inventory with its own lot.
kits.onlyFun: In the sample operation kits are assembled at CEDI Funza.
kits.note: The kit expires when its first-expiring component expires.

map.title: Warehouse map
map.subtitle: 96 locations (zone-aisle-bay) and 4 quarantine locations. Tap a location to see what is in it.
map.matches: {n, plural, =0 {No location matches} one {# location matches} other {# locations match}}
map.dockHint: The shipping dock is next to aisle P01 of zone A.
map.reservedBlock: It has units reserved for orders
map.expiredBlock: Expired lot: it cannot be released; write it off following your procedure.
map.note: The color comes from the product’s ABC class. Simplified sample layout; in your project your warehouse’s real layout is loaded.

stock.title: Stock by SKU
stock.subtitle: {wh}: available, reserved, blocked and to put away, with lots and stock card.
stock.expiringOnly: Only lots expiring in 30 days or less
stock.inDays: in {n, plural, =0 {today} one {# day} other {# days}}
stock.transferNote: In the demo the transfer is immediate. In your project it goes through shipping, transit and receiving at the destination warehouse.
stock.importText: Columns: sku; nombre (name); cliente (Lirio, Casa Tejo or Nutrilia); codigo_barras (optional); costo_unitario (unit cost); peso_kg; vence (si/no). Semicolon or comma separators are accepted.
stock.fileTooBig: The file is larger than 512 KB
stock.importNote: Products are created with no stock; they enter inventory when you receive them. In your project they are also synced from your ERP.
stock.note: Available = in good condition, not expired and not reserved for orders. Blocked = in quarantine or expired.

counts.title: ABC cycle counting
counts.subtitle: Products are classified by shipped value: class A is counted weekly, B monthly and C quarterly.
counts.accuracyHint: {match} of {total} counts with no difference (sample history + your counts)
counts.abcNote: The classification is calculated from the demand and cost of the sample products.
counts.tasksSubtitle: Blind count: you type what you count and then see the difference against the system.
counts.note: A shortage reported during picking creates an urgent count. Adjustments are recorded in the stock card with their value in pesos.

orders.title: Orders and waves
orders.subtitle: Orders from the 3PL’s clients by channel, with their cutoff time. Select them and release a wave.
orders.waveBar: {n, plural, =0 {No orders selected} one {# order selected} other {# orders selected}}
orders.noStock: None of the selected orders has enough stock
orders.released: Wave released with {n} orders: stock was reserved by FEFO
orders.releasedPartial: Wave released with {ok} orders; {failed} without enough stock stay to release
orders.note: The sample orders come from an online store, a marketplace and wholesale customers. In your project they come in through the integration with your store (Shopify, WooCommerce or VTEX), your marketplace or your ERP. Cutoff by channel: store 3:00 PM, marketplace 2:00 PM, wholesale 5:00 PM.
orders.noneDue: No order to release has today’s cutoff: they are all due tomorrow

picking.title: Picking
picking.subtitle: Route calculated for the wave according to the strategy. Change the strategy and compare distance and time.
picking.noWave: No waves in this warehouse. Release one from Orders.
picking.routeSubtitle: Dock → locations in aisle order → dock.
picking.routeAria: Simplified layout with the picking route
picking.routeNote: Distances calculated in the browser on a sample layout (1.6 m between bays and 3.2 m between aisles, at 50 m/min and 20 s per line).
picking.pickerSubtitle: This is how it looks on the picker’s phone or handheld.
picking.wrongProduct: That code is not this task’s product.
picking.wrongLoc: That is not this task’s location.
picking.shortToast: Shortage at {bin}: an urgent count was created and another lot was searched
picking.pickerNote: Works with a barcode scanner or by typing the code. The installable Android app with camera scanning is built in your project.

packing.queueSubtitle: Picked orders, sorted by cutoff time.
packing.none: No picked orders in this warehouse.
packing.notInOrder: That product is not in this order
packing.alreadyVerified: You already verified all units of {sku}
packing.shortNote: Shipped incomplete: {n} u. were short during picking.
packing.note: Label and tracking number simulated in the demo. In your project the label is created in the carrier’s system through its API (or a shipping aggregator) and printed on your thermal printer.

label.title: Shipping label · {guide}
label.note: The bars are illustrative (a scanner will not read them). In your project the label comes from the carrier (PDF or ZPL).

carriers.title: Carriers
carriers.subtitle: Sample rates from {wh} by destination zone. Mark the preferred one for this warehouse.
carriers.days: {n, plural, one {# business day} other {# business days}}
carriers.preferredSet: {name} is now the preferred carrier in {wh}
carriers.note: Fictitious carriers with sample rates in Colombian pesos. In your project we connect through APIs to the carriers you use (for example Servientrega, Coordinadora, Interrapidísimo, TCC, Envía or Deprisa) or through a shipping aggregator.
carriers.quoteNote: These are the same rules the packing station uses to suggest a carrier.

routes.title: Own-fleet routing · {wh}
routes.subtitle: Today’s deliveries in the metro area with time windows and capacity per vehicle.
routes.none: No own-fleet deliveries in this warehouse.
routes.kmHint: Out and back to the warehouse
routes.started: The route has left: it is not re-optimized
routes.alreadyBest: The current plan is already the best the heuristic found
routes.note: Heuristic calculated in your browser (sector sweep, nearest neighbor and 2-opt improvement) with straight-line distances × 1.3 at 25 km/h. Illustrative map without streets. In your project a routing engine with the real road network and traffic is used.

driver.title: Driver app
driver.subtitle: The vehicle’s route in plan order. Record arrival, delivery with proof or an exception.
driver.note: Preview of the driver’s mobile app inside the demo. Changes show up instantly in Tracking and on the Dashboard.
driver.photoError: The image could not be read
driver.podRequired: Type the name and get the signature to confirm.
driver.deliveredToast: Order {order} delivered with proof of delivery

tracking.title: Shipment tracking
tracking.subtitle: This warehouse’s labels with their timeline.
tracking.podCarrier: Proof of delivery reported by the carrier (simulated).
tracking.ownNote: Own fleet: the driver records the statuses in their app.
tracking.carrierNote: Events simulated in the demo. In your project they come from the carrier through an API or webhook.
tracking.whatsapp: Hi {name}, your order {order} from {client} has left our warehouse with {carrier}. Tracking no.: {guide}. Estimated delivery: {eta}.
tracking.etaDays: {n, plural, one {# business day} other {# business days}}
tracking.waNote: Nothing is sent in the demo. In your project it is sent through the WhatsApp Business Platform or by email when the status changes.

returns.newSubtitle: For orders delivered from this warehouse.
returns.noDelivered: No delivered orders in this warehouse.
returns.commentsPh: Product condition, what the customer says…
returns.formNote: The end customer and the 3PL client are stored separately.

seedComments.c1: The cap arrived broken and the product spilled.
seedComments.c2: They received a different item from the one they ordered.
seedComments.c3: They withdrew from the purchase within the allowed period.
seedComments.c4: The product failed on first use.
seedComments.c5: They changed their mind on the delivery day.
seedComments.c6: They reported it four months after the purchase.

returns.note: When received, the return enters the stock card and the map (restock or quarantine). The credit note and the refund are issued by your ERP or invoicing system; the WMS does not invoice.

billing.title: 3PL billing (pre-invoice)
billing.subtitle: Per-service billing for each 3PL client, with editable rates. Includes all three warehouses.
billing.prevNote: Previous month: sample volumes calculated with the daily average of the sample operation.
billing.mtdNote: Current month: previous days at the sample average + what you did today in the demo (picking, shipments and returns).
billing.erpNote: The WMS calculates the pre-invoice; the electronic invoice is issued by your ERP or your e-invoicing provider.
billing.sample: Sample document generated by the demo: it is not an invoice and has no tax validity.
